newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended a mostly quiet day lower, coming under late pressure after U.S. Treasury bond prices fell. But prices steadied above lows by the close.

U.S. Treasuries dipped by over a point after release of new U.S. data. U.S. durable goods orders rose by a stronger than expected 1.8 percent in July, and the Chicago Purchasing Management Association reported its August index rose to 60.0, up sharply from 51.2 in July.
The September confederate bond futures contract briefly fell sharply after the data, but recovered much of its losses before session end.

"It was a very, very, very quiet day with minimal volumes. We were five to 10 ticks lower in the longer maturities, and after the U.S. numbers we were 10 to 15 ticks lower," said one Swiss bond trader.
He said volume was generally fairly thin but that selling volume pick up as prices fell.
Shorter rates were steady to slightly lower.

Money market rates were quoted slightly easier after the Swiss National Bank added liquidity early in the day. Traders said it added four-month Swiss francs via swaps priced at 137 pips and also put in liquidity for two days below 2.00 percent.
Sept comi medium-term bond down five at 109.50.
Sept Euro Swiss francs steady at 97.80.
